A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KAPPA research, with matching title, authors, and central approach. All 31 pages of v2 and 18 pages of v3, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original probing, intervention, transfer, free-form generation, and general-capability results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark measurements, intervention comparisons, transfer analyses, and generation results in Sections 3–5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The two probes and minimum-perturbation affine alignment procedure remain unchanged. General k-option probing and intervention already appear in v2 Section 3.3 and Appendix C; their central placement in v3 does not introduce a new algorithm. The scale/offset mechanism is also retained.

E1.justification: v3 adds GSM8K, TruthfulQA, PubMedQA, and BBQ Age/Religion, substantially expanding mathematical, biomedical, truthfulness, and bias coverage. BBH and MMLU have revised subtask compositions, beyond category renaming. Free-form evaluation changes from BBH to TruthfulQA, BBQ-Age, and GSM8K, while v2's vicuna-eval coverage is removed.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates logistic-regression steering, LoRA fine-tuning, and BM25-based ICL. v3 replaces these comparisons with difference-in-means CAA and DoLA, reported in Tables 2–3 and 11–12. CAA is procedurally different from v2's steering baseline. These comparators also enter general-MCQ comparisons where v2 Table 3 reported only Base, KAPPA, and the knowledge probe.

E3.justification: v3 adds KLD as an evaluation metric; agreement was already measured in v2 Appendix G. It introduces an 85% prediction-probe accuracy threshold for layer selection and changes the general-MCQ multilayer scale from 20 to 10, retaining the single-layer value of 30. General-MCQ evaluation gains six-layer configurations. The primary Llama model changes from Llama-2-7B to Llama-3.1-8B, and broader-model tests replace Qwen3-32B with Qwen3-14B and add Mistral-7B.

E4.justification: v3 adds a subtask analysis of which errors cross-dataset transfer corrects, testing whether transfer follows shared reasoning skills (Figure 6). The parameter sweep changes from BBH-Binary accuracy to TruthfulQA agreement. v2's separate-subtask probing/intervention analyses, transformed-state comparison, explicit MCQ/free-form mismatch check, and general-capability preservation evaluation are removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. Answer-order permutations and v2's swapped-response judging are evaluation controls rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Substantial result sets are replaced or added. v2 Table 1 reports Llama-2 BBH-Binary accuracy increasing from 50.9% to 70.8%; v3 Table 2 instead includes Llama-3.1 TruthfulQA results of 56.7% to 73.5% with three-layer KAPPA. v3 also reports mixed free-form outcomes, including GSM8K declining from 91.6% to 90.7% (Table 4). Changed tasks, models, and settings preclude interpreting these as performance changes under identical conditions across versions.

T1.justification: The general k-option Lagrange derivation is retained from v2 Appendix C in v3 Appendix B.1, while the separate binary derivation and rank-one LoRA decomposition disappear. However, v3 Appendix B.2 substitutes a matrix into v2's scalar norm-based projection expression. This is not generally equivalent to the inverse-Gram solution for multiple independent directions, introducing a localized mathematical inconsistency.

C1.justification: v3 makes systematic gap quantification and differences between reasoning, truthfulness/bias, and knowledge benchmarks central contributions. It replaces v2's broad domain-general transfer message with partial transfer between tasks sharing skills. The central claim that geometric intervention can align predictions with encoded knowledge is retained.

C2.justification: v3 introduces hypotheses linking truthfulness/bias gaps to hasty answering and reasoning gaps to underused representations without intermediate traces. It interprets limited transfer through shared skills and acknowledges restricted free-form benefits when generation is already strong. Its discussion also makes the boundary around linearly accessible knowledge more explicit and identifies nonlinear knowledge alignment as unresolved.

D1.justification: v3 Appendix C newly documents probe batch size 128, checkpoint selection across 1000 epochs, and detailed CAA construction and DoLA configuration. v2's explicit intervention-layer tables and extensive generation-evaluation specifications disappear. In particular, v3 names GPT-4o-mini without retaining v2's dated judge identifier or full answer-matching prompt. Both versions retain the same promise to release code upon publication.

R1.justification: v3 substantially revises positioning toward systematic MCQ-gap measurement and connecting gap detection with mitigation. It adds discussion of MCQ evaluation failures, hidden factual knowledge, arithmetic probing, and decoding approaches, citing works such as Balepur et al., Goral et al., Gekhman et al., Sun et al., and Chuang et al. The dedicated fine-tuning/LoRA contrast and associated references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and empirical narrative are extensively rewritten. v2's binary-first Method/Experiments organization becomes separate sections on measuring the gap, geometric analysis, intervention, and further analysis. The general-MCQ formulation leads the exposition, and the appendices are substantially consolidated and reorganized.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column to a two-column layout. The motivating and pipeline diagrams are redesigned into a combined schematic. Tables gain grouped accuracy/agreement/KLD columns, and new scatter plots, a transfer heatmap, and subtask charts replace much of the previous visual presentation. Several detailed appendix heatmaps and tables are removed.

improvement.justification: v3 better connects the central alignment claim to direct gap measurements and inference-time comparisons on general MCQs. Its explicit account of limited transfer also improves on v2's broad generalization claims. These benefits are tempered by the newly inconsistent matrix projection expression in Appendix B.2, reduced generation-judging reproducibility, and improvement language that remains broader than some results in Tables 11–12 support. The net quality gain is therefore limited.
